scope: Serialized radio controller, durable transition ownership and Wi-Fi-only D-Bus adapter, with read-only native probes. No runtime radio control, session admission or installation service integration is enabled.

validation.artifact_source: ARM debug binaries built from the clean implementation_head; host tests used the identical source before its commit. Not a packaged runtime image.

properties_exercised: Default Off leaves independently disabled Wi-Fi alone. Policy-owned off state persists and is restored on disabling the mode; Stay connected survives service restart and a clean reboot can rebase profile revision counters.
Time-check and download holds use existing Ethernet without waking Wi-Fi. Setup requires wireless availability; no response asserts Internet access or Wi-Fi association.
A concurrent hold queues behind a blocked off command and is acknowledged only after restoration. Failed restoration, missing readback and expiry during restoration cannot acknowledge availability.
Unknown or live activity, hardware/startup/checkpoint conditions and unavailable guards prevent shutdown. Activity introduced during guard acquisition is rechecked.
Observed external radio/profile/manager changes persist suspension until explicit reconciliation. A known unsent command may retry; an ambiguous dispatched command cannot be cleared in the same boot.

Flush failures before dispatch never send a command; a record published before the failure remains uncertain after reopen. A returned command can complete from later matching readback, but a mismatching reply cannot claim ownership.
An actual private D-Bus server verifies the Wi-Fi-only property write, unique-owner/profile checks, permission denial and a command that applies after the caller times out.

The probe compares bounded sorted per-connection VersionId inventories around coherent radio reads. Missing/malformed properties, profile inventory/revision changes, duplicates, invalid paths and oversized inventories cannot imply stable state.
Read-only probes succeeded on both installed root-owned NetworkManager instances from UID 1000. Pi fixtures used temporary files and a private D-Bus daemon.

device_api_discovery.initial_probe_result: Failed because the top-level Settings object has no VersionId property. Read-only busctl checks on both devices confirmed the missing property.
device_api_discovery.correction: Read Connections on Settings, then VersionId on each Settings.Connection. Hash sorted paths and counters; never read settings or secrets. Fixtures now model the actual runtime interface.

limits: serve does not yet instantiate this controller or expose network control/hold requests. No runtime off path is enabled.

Native SSH/session admission, install guards, continuous external radio-change monitoring and expected setup-profile changes still require integration. Fixture activity/guards do not qualify real SSH races.
A new-boot profile counter baseline does not prove profiles stayed unchanged while the service was absent. Radio changes reversed between polling snapshots still need the continuous observer.
Setup/deployment lease hooks, offline scheduling, the downloader, install policy, production signing/feed and physical Pi recovery qualification remain outstanding.

No installed services, radio settings, credentials, data partitions, root/boot files or watchdog were modified. Neither probe rebooted its target; each recorded boot ID stayed unchanged during its run.
Earlier bootstrap runtime/kits do not contain this networking implementation. Root connection details and supervised device bootstrap remain pending.
The overall auto-update goal is incomplete.
